text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Amsterdam stock exchange at a new high at 639.09 (p1).
- Electricity producers and distibutors, economic affairs ministry and Amsterdam bourses expect a electricity futures exchange to open on January 1 1998. (p1)
- Full conversion to average-wage pension scheme would result in one to two percent cut in pension premiums within three years. (p1)
- Container transshipment company Europe Combined Terminals sees number of container movements in 1996 drop "marginally". (p3)
- Publisher Wegener Arcade buys France's record label Flarensch. (p3)
- Publisher Reed Elsevier is switching to electronic publishing at high speed but Elsevier Business Information's new chief still sees ample potential for paper publications. (p3)
- ABN AMRO sets up a 50-50 joint venture in Uzbekistan with a local partner. (p4)
- Dutch Bureau for Credit registration BKR talks with Belgium's Nationale Bank on possibilities for data exchange. (p13)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Automation company Baan considers boost to current growth percentage next year. (p2)
- European issues manual to stimulate EU countries to more environmentally friendly production. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Police and justice's drive against illegal fireworks is beginning to show results. (p1)
- Province of Friesland is gearing up for the traditional ice-skating race over the lakes between 11 towns. (p1)
- Members of parliament do not know Dutch history very well, or so it appears from a telephone poll. (p3)
TROUW
- Chiefs of police on Antillean island Aruba to challenge their dismissal. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Amsterdam reddies itself ready for June Euro summit. (p4)
